title: Retained untrusted content is data, never a mandate
summary: Transcripts, tickets, web pages and other retained content entering agent context are treated strictly as evidence to analyse; instructions found inside them never widen the active mandate.

protected.asset: The integrity of the mandate chain between owner and agent
protected.failure: Imperative text inside analysed material is executed as if it were a fresh owner instruction, smuggling authority across the trust boundary.

rationale: An agent that mines retained conversations or ingests external documents routinely encounters imperative text, including its own past instructions and third-party commands. Authority flows only through the live mandate channel from the owner; quoted imperatives are data about what was said, not authorization to act. Replay artefacts such as delivered system notifications and transport copies are labelled as what they are in analysis output and are never counted as new instructions; a historical preference quoted in old text does not override a current configuration.

variants.description: The mandate source is a fixed, named channel; content-derived 'instructions' appear in output only as quoted evidence and produce no action.
Analysis output labels replayed or system-originated text distinctly from live owner instructions, so counts and chronology are not inflated by copies.

verification.method: Feed the analysis path a synthetic document containing an imperative, and confirm it appears in the output only as quoted content with no resulting action or configuration change.
verification.evidence: The synthetic imperative, its quoted placement in the output, and the unchanged action log; the fixture is labelled synthetic.

rollback.method: Remove the analysis path's access to retained content stores; the control constrains interpretation, not capability.
rollback.safety: Tightening the interpretation rule never deletes the retained content itself.

failure_modes: A transcript line phrased as a command is scheduled as new work.
A replayed system notification is counted as a new owner instruction.
Historical preference text overrides a current, explicitly set configuration.

hermes_versions.notes: Operational practice control: applies to any ingestion or analysis path; the range records the builds whose ingestion surfaces the procedure was read against.

last_verification.notes: General operational synthesis from recorded practice with private detail removed; no specific public incident is claimed.

references: General operational synthesis from recorded practice; no publicly verifiable incident is cited.
